In the central binary case, e_Q(J)≤e_B(J)2^(t d₂(J)); a faithful cover of B of degree v gives Σ_J e_Q(J)^ell≤s_(b+ell(v+2t)), with deterministic source-dependent torsor origins recovered.

claims.statement: Let T be an actual transitive 2-group of degree s=2^a, A a section of its permutation module, S=A^B, t=dim S, and L the retained annihilator. A rank-r space W of point-stabilizer characters whose common kernel has 2^j orbits satisfies t+ell_W≤2^j binom(a−j,floor((a−j)/2)). The joint rank spectrum obeys Σ_(dim W=r)(2^ell_W−1)=Σ_q R_q [d−q choose r−q]_2.

For retained L≤H⊗S of dimension ell and maximum rank-one multiplicity j0, q evaluations separate L with q≤min(t,floor((ell+max(1,j0))/2)). Their common kernel C has cost 2t+2q. The joint budget gives cost≤2B_a+2B_(a−1)≤15s/16 for s=2^a≥64, where B_i=binom(i,floor(i/2)).

For the actual retained rank counts R_r, Xi_c=Σ_r R_r[t−r choose c−r]_2/[t choose c]_2<1 implies an actual c-dimensional C≤S annihilating the retained incidence, with residual rank t−c. This is a nonnegative-integer expectation argument on one common cut.

For a degree-32 top, the extreme case t=ell=10 satisfies 15R1+R2≤465, 15R1+7R2+3R3+R4≤1953, and ΣR_q=1023. The exact dual gives Xi_5≤103925485/109221651<1, hence cost 30 and a degree-32 cover, total 62<64. For a degree-16 top, d(H0)≤3 gives cost≤14 with the original cover v0=16; d(H0)=4 forces T=B=E16, allowing a faithful degree-8 cover and cost≤18. The degree-16-top cases therefore satisfy v0+2c+4r(A/C)≤30 with v0 in {8,16}.

For a full peel 1→N→K→L→1 of finite 2-groups inside L×G, set k=d_G(N), n=log₂|N|, and m=max d_G(B) over normal B≤N∩G′. Then delta=d(K)−d(L) and epsilon=max(0,rho(K)−rho(L)) satisfy 0≤delta≤k, 0≤epsilon≤m, delta+epsilon≤n. With a2=d_G(N²[N,G]), the positive tau increment is at most k−delta+a2. Use q=max(m,a2). The separate tau transport is valid for arbitrary finite groups with Phi₂(G)=G′G².

claims.statement: The necessary high relative-3-rank actions are natural C3/A4, 6T1/4/5/6, 12T20/85/164/194/228/229/265, and degree-9 or degree-27 3-groups. The index-two ternary consumer accepts 6T1/5; the affine consumer accepts 6T4; the cyclic-module consumer accepts 6T6 and 12T85/164; the prime-base cyclic-module consumer accepts 12T20/194; the conditional degree-12 V4-base consumer accepts 12T228/229/265; the conditional degree-9 consumer accepts the actual degree-9 3-groups; and the ternary tail accepts the degree-27 3-groups. All conditional tests retain the original orbit pattern.
